# Exemptions for scripts/privacy-guard.mjs. The guard reads this file from the base (main's
# tip), so a pull request that adds an exemption gets it only after that pull request has
# merged. A waiting pull request gets it on its next run, with no merge of main.
# The guard flags a change to this file, its script or its workflow: read every line.
#
#   email <domain-or-address>     an address, or a domain and its subdomains
#   path <glob> <rule,rule | *>   the named rules are not applied to matching files
#   repo <name>                   a private repository whose name public files may use
#   product <Name>                a public product name the private-repo rule would otherwise
#                                 flag. Exact spelling and case, and a capital letter in it. Only
#                                 the bare word, in prose: see isProductName in privacy-guard.mjs.
#   site <domain>                 a public site whose domain is also a private repository's name.
#                                 The owner's rule of record (20 November 2026): "we can name public
#                                 website URLs even if the repo and code is private." So the line
#                                 itself, which says that this domain is a private repository's name,
#                                 is accepted in writing: it is not read for its own domain, and
#                                 a repository with no allowlist adds its first one by itself. It
#                                 clears nothing else in the push. Word the commit message without
#                                 the name: messages are read. Web TLDs only (com, net, org, io, ca,
#                                 co, app, dev, fm, me, info, xyz, music, studio, art, it, ai, uk,
#                                 tv, band, shop).
#                                 Host form only: write https://<domain>/... with the scheme. Also
#                                 fine: an attribute or bracket (href="//<domain>"), an address
#                                 (booking@<domain>, not git@), site:<domain> and _<domain>_. A bare
#                                 domain with a path (<domain>/albums) is refused: it reads as a
#                                 directory of the repository. A line is refused when, with every URL
#                                 and the domain taken out, it says visibility, or that something is
#                                 private (is, still, stays private; private ending a clause), or
#                                 holds repo, repository, codebase, internal, gorfednet, clone,
#                                 checkout, pnpm, npm, gh or confidential, or an identifier that joins
#                                 those in any case or spelling (REPO_NAME, repoName, REPONAME,
#                                 isPrivate, REPO1, secret_key, PRNumber); or when the name is followed
#                                 by #12, PR, CI or issue, or follows cd, clone, checkout or -R.
#                                 Prose is fine: GitHub, source, org, remote, git, private events,
#                                 Secret show, the gate, PR contact, a CI badge. privateKey,
#                                 PrivateRoute and visibilityState are other things.
#                                 Accepted as written, each already disclosed by the allowlist line
#                                 itself: a // after . } or " (cd ..//<domain>), cd or git -C not
#                                 directly before the name, and a JSON or table row that names the site.
#                                 Listing a name the base already says puts it back on watch: a branch
#                                 named after it, or name.git, then refuses. See isPublicSite.
#   commit <sha>                  a commit (the full 40 hex) whose own diff and message are exempt.
#                                 A pushed commit cannot be rewritten, so this clears a false
#                                 positive in one that is not the tip. The net diff is still read.
#
# Rules: private-ip, session-id, tailnet-name, internal-host, private-repo, email,
# owner-quote, new-file. The reserved example domains need no line: they are built in.

# Public workflows and scripts here read the private ops repository by design, and its
# name is already in dozens of files. The pull request check's secret leaves it out; this
# line does the same for the local pre-push hook, which lists every private repository.
repo ops

# Public product names.
product MoonMan
product BinderCurve

# Test fixtures hold planted bad values on purpose. Only this directory, so a folder
# named fixtures somewhere else is not a way round the guard.
path test/fixtures/** *

commit b642bd39924c04e50b4ef17894fe417045b16464
